name: Back to Basics 2
source: written 28 Aug 2026. Level 2 of three. Same six shapes as level 1 at the next rung, and the first level where HOW you do a rep is part of the prescription.
entryIf: You can do 3 × 10 bodyweight squats, 3 × 8 push-ups from the floor and hold a 30 second plank without the hips dropping. If any of those is a maybe, level 1 first.

methods.name: Tempo
methods.what: A count on the way down. 3-1-1 is three seconds lowering, one at the bottom, one up.
methods.why: Time under load without more load. The cheapest way to make a movement harder while it is still being learned.

methods.name: Pause
methods.what: A full stop at the hardest position, then move.
methods.why: Kills the bounce. What is left is what you can actually do.

methods.name: Unilateral
methods.why: The strong side stops covering for the weak one. This is where most people find out.

methods.name: Superset
methods.what: Two movements back to back, one rest after the pair.
methods.why: More work in the same half hour, without turning it into conditioning.

constraints.time: 30 minutes, three days. The extra ten minutes over level 1 is the tempo, not more exercises.

goals: Own the six shapes at full range and under control
Find the weak side and stop hiding it
Hold a tempo without counting out loud by week 4
Arrive at level 3 able to be tested

d1.name: Squat & Push
d1.why: Same day as level 1, done properly. The squat gets a three second lower and a pause at the bottom, which is where the honest version of the movement lives. The push-up comes off the counter and onto the floor.

blocks.name: A · Goblet Squat, tempo
blocks.note: 4 × 8, tempo 3-1-1, rest 90s. Three down, one at the bottom, one up. Stop the set when the tempo goes, not when the reps do.

items.note: 90s rest · tempo 3-1-1 · elbows inside the knees at the bottom

blocks.name: B · Push-Up + Ring Row
blocks.note: B1 into B2 with no rest, then 75s. Two shapes in one block.

items.note: superset B1 · from the floor. Knees down for the last reps beats stopping at six.
superset B2 · walk the feet forward to make it harder

blocks.name: C · Single-Leg Bridge
blocks.note: 3 × 10 each side, rest 45s. One side at a time.

items.note: 45s rest · hips stay level. The side that shakes is the side that needed this.
Knees bent is still the right version if the back lifts.

d2.name: Hinge & Pull
d2.why: The hinge takes load for the first time and the pull moves toward a bar. The RDL keeps the strictest rule in the program: the set ends the rep the back changes shape.

items.note: Hang, pull the shoulders down, arms stay straight.

blocks.name: A · Romanian Deadlift, paused
blocks.note: 4 × 8, rest 90s. Pause one second at the bottom of every rep — the stretch is the point, the bounce is not.

items.note: 90s rest · 1s pause at the bottom · the set ends the rep the back rounds

blocks.name: B · Wide Inverted Row
blocks.note: 4 × 8, rest 75s. Lower the bar as it gets easier.

items.note: 75s rest · chest to the bar, body in one line

blocks.name: C · Suitcase Carry
blocks.note: 3 rounds of 40 seconds per side, rest 45s. One weight — the point is the side that is not holding it.

items.note: 45s rest · do not let the ribs tip

d3.name: Full Body
d3.why: The day that puts it together. A superset opens it, a unilateral squat finds the weak leg, and it closes on a carry — the shape nobody trains and everybody needs.

blocks.name: A · Kettlebell Swing + Push-Up
blocks.note: A1 into A2, no rest, then 75s. Fast then slow — the swing is hips, the push-up is control.

items.note: superset A1 · snap the hips, the bell floats
superset A2 · slow down, one count up

blocks.name: B · Bulgarian Split Squat
blocks.note: 3 × 8 each side, rest 75s. Back foot on a bench. This is the one that tells you the truth.

items.note: 75s rest · front foot takes the weight, knee tracks the toes

blocks.name: C · Hip Thrust
blocks.note: 3 × 12, rest 60s. Squeeze and hold a second at the top.

items.note: 60s rest · 1s hold at the top, ribs down
45s rest · heavy enough that the last ten seconds are honest
